newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trades only once, no bids posted at close.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trades only once, no bids posted at close.

text.p: The modest revival on the IPE's natural gas futures contract continued on Thursday morning, as 25 lots were traded in a single deal.
The trade was done in September, which slipped marginally - by a mere 0.015 pence a therm - to 11.70 pence.

But bids and offers were still few and far between. By the close of the morning session, no bids were posted at all. But the first 10 months, from June to next March, were all offered at levels above the previous settlement price.

The contract has been through a lean period recently, with no trade done for several sessions between Friday morning and Wednesday afternoon. But for most of that time there were at least some bids and offers posted, and the exchange as well as many brokers remained confident that trade was going to pick up again.

The trade drought broke just before the contract closed on Wednesday, when three deals totalling 30 lots were done. Thursday morning's deal, though welcome to market participants, is still only the fourth of the week.
"We're obviously pleased to see trading resume," said a spokeswoman for the IPE, but she added that the exchange was not surprised at the restart.
The exchange had been concerned by the lack of trade and had made enquiries of several participants, all of whom said the trade halt would not last long.
